title: Electronic Structure of Atoms - Chemistry - Electron Config
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the correct ground-state electron configuration for Carbon (atomic number 6)?
questions.explain: Carbon has 6 electrons. Filling order: $1s$ (2 electrons), $2s$ (2 electrons), remaining 2 go into $2p$. Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which is the correct electron configuration for Calcium ($Ca$, $Z=20$) using noble gas notation?
questions.explain: The noble gas preceding Calcium is Argon ($Ar$, 18 electrons). Calcium has 20 electrons, so the remaining 2 go into the $4s$ orbital. Notation: $[Ar] 4s^2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the full electron configuration for Iron ($Fe$, $Z=26$)?
questions.explain: Iron has 26 electrons. Order: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 3d^6$. Note that while $4s$ fills before $3d$, standard writing convention often groups shells by principal quantum number, but option (a) and (d) are chemically equivalent in content. ExamOven standard often accepts the filling order or the principal shell order. $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 3d^6$ correctly accounts for all electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which neutral element has the electron configuration $[Ar] 4s^2 3d^{10} 4p^5$?
questions.explain: Argon is 18 electrons. $18 + 2 (4s) + 10 (3d) + 5 (4p) = 35$ electrons. Element 35 is Bromine ($Br$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How many valence electrons does an atom of Sulfur ($S​$, Group 16) possess?
questions.explain: Sulfur is in Group 16. Its configuration is $[Ne] 3s^2 3p^4$. The valence electrons are those in the outermost shell ($n=3$): $2 + 4 = 6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the correct electron configuration for the Iron(II) ion, $Fe^{2+}$?
questions.explain: When transition metals form cations, they lose electrons from the highest $s​$ orbital first. $Fe$ is $[Ar] 4s^2 3d^6$. Removing two electrons from the $4s$ orbital leaves $[Ar] 3d^6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The oxide ion ($O^{2-}$) is isoelectronic with which noble gas?
questions.explain: Oxygen ($Z=8$) gains 2 electrons to form $O^{2-}$, resulting in 10 electrons. Neon ($Z=10$) has 10 electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Identify the element with the ground state electron configuration ending in $5p^3$.
questions.explain: An element ending in $5p^3$ is in Period 5, Group 15. Looking at the periodic table, this element is Antimony ($Sb$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which general electron configuration represents the valence shell of Group 2 (Alkaline Earth Metals) elements?
questions.explain: Group 2 elements have 2 valence electrons in their outermost $s​$ subshell. The general form is $ns^2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Scandium forms a $Sc^{3+}$ ion. What is the electron configuration of this ion?
questions.explain: Scandium ($Z=21$) is $[Ar] 4s^2 3d^1$. To form $Sc^{3+}$, it loses all 3 valence electrons ($2​$ from $4s$, $1​$ from $3d$), resulting in the configuration of Argon ($[Ar]$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the total number of electrons in $p​$ orbitals for a ground-state atom of Phosphorus ($P​$, $Z=15$)?
questions.explain: Phosphorus config: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3$. Electrons in $p​$ orbitals: $6​$ (from $2p$) + $3​$ (from $3p$) = $9​$ total electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which pair of species is **isoelectronic** (having the same number of electrons)?
questions.explain: Potassium ($K​$, $Z=19$) loses 1 electron to become $K^+$ (18 electrons). Argon ($Ar$, $Z=18$) has 18 electrons. Thus, they are isoelectronic.
